trends.title: From climate risk maps to anticipatory action
trends.summary: Connect hazard observations and forecasts to response decisions, resilient assets and pre-arranged finance.
trends.whyNow: 2026 announcements connect flood observation, predictive models, insurance workflows and farm protection. The practical question is whether better signals reach a funded decision or payout in time.
trends.application: prioritise exposed schools and clinics, rehearse early-action protocols or assess parametric cover for a defined hazard.
trends.experiment: Back-test a single hazard and district using historical events, local loss data and the exact decision or payout trigger.
trends.measure: Measure warning lead time, missed events, false alarms, exposure coverage and basis risk.
watchouts: Forecast error, poorly mapped assets and basis risk can create false confidence. Long-term scenario loss estimates need transparent assumptions; local institutions must be able to act on alerts.

trends.title: Software and finance for distributed energy
trends.summary: Use demand forecasting, remote operations and financing infrastructure to expand solar, storage and minigrids.
trends.whyNow: Mission 300 increases the relevance of distributed systems, while provider continuity and open metering options become material operating questions. New financing initiatives are emerging, including funds still being raised.
trends.application: improve minigrid site assessment, benchmark operating reliability or assess whether financing reaches underserved households and businesses.
trends.experiment: Compare forecast and repayment performance on a documented pilot portfolio; stress-test tariffs, defaults, downtime and productive-use demand.
trends.measure: Measure reliability, delivered energy cost, service affordability, repayment fairness and additional connections.
watchouts: Tariff affordability and maintenance capacity
Currency and repayment risks
Dependence on a single equipment or cloud provider
Groundwater and other productive-use externalities

trends.title: AI that reaches the farm decision
trends.summary: Combine crop and weather evidence with the finance, inputs and services needed to act on a farm.
trends.whyNow: Providers increasingly combine agronomic information with credit, input delivery, irrigation and insurance. New conversational systems need evidence that recommendations produce better local decisions.
trends.application: improve extension triage, crop monitoring and smallholder risk management with local agronomists and farmer feedback.
trends.experiment: Choose one crop and district; compare an assisted advisory workflow with the current practice through a season, using approved recommendations.
trends.measure: Measure advice accuracy, adoption, service cost and agronomic outcomes with a suitable comparison group.
watchouts: Images and satellite data may not generalise to local crops or plots. Mistaken treatment advice, weather uncertainty, data ownership and insurance basis risk need field testing.

trends.title: Adaptive foundational learning with teachers
trends.summary: Digital practice and teacher analytics that adapt to a learner's progress in bounded skills such as mathematics or early literacy.
trends.whyNow: Messaging-based tutoring can reach ordinary phones, and a 2026–27 Ghana trial is testing one approach at greater scale. Independent learning evidence should guide deployment, not conversational fluency.
trends.application: Help teachers target practice and support without assuming that every child has a connected personal device or that a general chatbot is an effective tutor.
trends.experiment: Choose a curriculum-matched learning unit and compare equivalent instructional time using independent assessments, with documented teacher support and device access.
trends.measure: Independent learning improvement, continued use, teacher workload, participation gaps, implementation fidelity and full recurring cost per learner.
watchouts: Curriculum and language mismatch
Children's data and accessibility
Implementation effects mistaken for model effects
Vendor learning-gain claims that do not transfer

trends.title: Reusable public infrastructure connects services and payments
trends.summary: Shared registries, service components and interoperable payment infrastructure allow institutions to build connected services without recreating every foundation.
trends.whyNow: Credential standards and implementation tools continue to mature; recent release candidates make browser-based verification tangible. Inclusive delivery still needs governance, alternatives and reliable local operations.
trends.application: Assess how a public service can use shared identity, records and payment capabilities while retaining clear institutional responsibility, exception handling and accessible channels.
trends.experiment: Build one synthetic service journey in a sandbox: verify a record, calculate an authorized charge or benefit, route a simulated payment and reconcile the result. Deliberately test missing records and interrupted transactions.
trends.measure: Reusable components, integration effort, reconciliation accuracy, exception recovery and ability to switch or extend providers; never infer country readiness from a working demo.
watchouts: Operating governance matters as much as code
Open source does not remove implementation cost
Exclusion through missing or mismatched records
Privacy, access controls and payment-scheme rules
trends.evidenceLabel: Open-source public-good platforms; local deployment requires implementation and governance

trends.title: Digitally enabled primary care
trends.summary: Support health workers with usable patient information, accessible diagnostics and dependable medicine delivery.
trends.whyNow: Service access depends on logistics and continuity of patient records as well as clinical software. Current deployments and expansion agreements provide concrete workflows to assess.
trends.application: assess supervised screening, clinic digitisation or pooled procurement against a locally defined care bottleneck.
trends.experiment: Pick one pathway and measure the whole journey: referral, diagnosis, treatment access and follow-up, alongside a clinician-reviewed evaluation.
trends.measure: Measure time to appropriate care, missed follow-up, service availability and total cost; evaluate clinical sensitivity and specificity where relevant.
watchouts: Clinical validation and applicable approvals are setting- and product-specific. Bias, privacy, workforce capacity, medicine quality and referral capacity affect real outcomes.

trends.title: Digital operating tools for productive small firms
trends.summary: Accessible devices, digital payments, records and sales channels help small businesses participate in markets and manage daily operations.
trends.whyNow: The WBG’s November 2026 MSME analysis emphasizes digital records, market connections and access to finance. Integrated merchant services offer operational use cases with measurable costs and benefits.
trends.application: Examine the bottleneck for a particular group of firms before choosing technology: accepting payments, maintaining stock records, reaching guests or obtaining a usable connected device.
trends.experiment: Follow a small consenting cohort through one complete operating cycle. Compare time, errors, net costs and business outcomes with its previous practice, including continued manual or offline options.
trends.measure: Active use, reconciliation or stock errors, staff time, net selling costs and earnings after fees and financing; separate growth from seasonal demand changes.
watchouts: Total fees and financing cost
Platform dependence and data portability
Connectivity and support burden
Adoption does not establish additional jobs
trends.evidenceLabel: Existing commercial services; proposed development applications

trends.title: Water systems that detect and respond
trends.summary: Sensors and analytics help operators find losses and manage demand; distributed technologies can supplement drinking-water supply in specific settings.
trends.whyNow: Providers connect sensor alerts to repair teams and farm decisions to basin accounting. Useful evidence measures completed repairs and net water outcomes, not only algorithmic detection.
trends.application: test a leak-to-repair workflow with a utility; separately assess distributed drinking-water supply only where lifecycle economics make sense.
trends.experiment: Instrument a small zone, verify suspected leaks in the field and compare water recovered with the full intervention cost.
trends.measure: Measure verified water recovered, false positives, repair time, energy use and cost per cubic metre.
watchouts: Detection creates value only if repairs happen. Sensor maintenance, network maps and connectivity are constraints. Atmospheric water is site-dependent and is not a replacement for bulk municipal supply.

trends.title: Digital measurement for nature and carbon
trends.summary: Combine satellites, models and field samples to estimate carbon stocks and changes and support independent verification.
trends.whyNow: Issued soil-carbon credits are reaching buyers, alongside growing digital measurement capabilities. Transaction volume should be assessed separately from additionality, permanence, land rights and independent assurance.
trends.application: compare evidence for forest restoration or soil-carbon projects, with transparent uncertainty and community data rights.
trends.experiment: Blind-test two providers against independent field measurements and a clearly specified accounting boundary; keep verification separate from project sales.
trends.measure: Measure uncertainty, reproducibility, coverage, total monitoring cost and agreement with independent reference data.
watchouts: Digital estimates do not establish additionality, permanence or rights by themselves. Model bias, baselines, sampling and verification independence remain material.
